title: AI Startup Disseqt AI Raises $8 Mn To Scale International Operations
summary: Disseqt AI raises 8 million dollars to expand its AI governance and testing agents globally
detailed: Disseqt AI raised $8 million in a funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, Enterprise Ireland, and angel investor Rahul Dravid.
The startup builds independent governance and testing platforms for enterprise AI agents to ensure safety, fairness, and policy compliance prior to deployment.
Headquartered in Ireland with engineering teams in Bengaluru, Disseqt plans to use the capital to scale operations across the UK and international markets.
The company has partnered with major Indian IT firms including Infosys, Cognizant, and HCLTech as Global System Integrators.
sentences: Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners, and Enterprise Ireland also participated in the round, along with angel investors like cricketer Rahul Dravid and senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce, and Meta.
The startup plans to use the fresh capital to expand its global enterprise customer base and scale operations across the UK and international markets.
“Every enterprise is handing real work to AI agents, but very few can prove those agents are safe, fair and within policy.

This gap often stops ambitious AI projects from going live, and it is what we built Disseqt to close … This funding lets us bring that standard to more enterprises around the world,” said CEO and cofounder Apoorva Kumar.
Founded in late 2025 by Kumar, Manish Atri, and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt operates an independent governance and testing layer for enterprise AI agents.
Essentially, it ensures that AI systems are behaving as intended and meet regulatory requirements.
The platform enables compliance, security, and IT teams to test agentic workflows for vulnerabilities and data-leak risks prior to deployment.
It can enforce real-time policy guardrails in production, block non-compliant outputs, and maintain audit trails independent of underlying model providers.
While its commercial operations and headquarters are in Ireland, Disseqt’s engineering and AI teams are based in Bengaluru.
It has customer-facing operations across the UK, Ireland and India, according to its website.
Atri, its COO, is also India-based.
Both Kumar and Atri are graduates of IIIT Allahabad.

Besides, it has also partnered with major Indian IT companies like Infosys, Cognizant, HCLTech, Mphasis, and Tata Technologies as ‘Global System Integrators’ to deploy its platforms for their enterprise clients.
This adds to the uptick in investor interest in AI startups.
As per Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, AI startup funding more than tripled YoY to $438 Mn in the September quarter.
The surging investor interest in AI comes even as the overall funding landscape remains relatively subdued, with the cumulative funding raised by Indian startups increasing by just 5% YoY.
